rationale: Lyc. action-noun ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- (cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ 'the dissolution,' ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ†ⲟⲩⲱ 'the raising' in glossary) on ⲭⲧⲟ = ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, give birth.' Designates the generative act applied both to Adam's primordial begetting and to ordinary human reproduction. Distinguished from homophonous ⲕⲧⲟ 'turn, return.'
Lyc. action-noun ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- + ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'give birth.' Parallel formation to ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲭⲧⲟ but on the alternate begetting-verb ⲙⲓⲥⲉ. Used interchangeably in the same passage.

Lycopolitan plural of ⲣⲟⲙⲡⲉ 'year,' regularly with ⲕⲉ- prefix 'other (years).' Already tentatively in accumulated vocabulary; this page confirms the plural form and the idiomatic ⲕⲉⲣⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲉⲩⲉ for one's lifespan-of-many-years.

Qualitative or stative form related to ⲇⲱⲭⲃⲉ 'diminish' (already in glossary) and ϩⲟⲁⲭⲃⲉ 'is lesser' — Lyc. orthographic variant. Predicates the smallness/diminution of present-day human stature and lifespan compared with Adam's.

proposed_english: spend years / live (a number of) years
rationale: Verbal idiom ⲣ̄- ('do, make') + ⲣⲁⲙⲡⲉ ('year') = 'spend years, pass years.' With quantifier ⲁϩ 'many' = 'spend many years.' Standard Coptic temporal-duration construction.

Greek πλατύνω 'widen, spread' (already in accumulated vocabulary) + Lyc. ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' The directional compound conveys the centrifugal scattering action — paired here with ⲭⲣⲁⲣⲱⲱϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'scatter forth' as Sin's twin scattering-actions on the disciples.
